question: What directional relationship do yellow center line markings and white lane line markings communicate?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The color of a longitudinal line communicates the directional relationship of the traffic it separates. Yellow center line markings delineate the separation of traffic lanes that have opposite directions of travel, while white lane line markings delineate the separation of traffic lanes that have the same direction of travel. In short, yellow means opposing traffic is on the other side of the line; white means traffic on both sides is moving the same way. Standards (mandatory): - "Center line pavement markings, when used, shall be the pavement markings used to delineate the separation of traffic lanes that have opposite directions of travel on a roadway and shall be yellow." - "When used, lane line pavement markings delineating the separation of traffic lanes that have the same direction of travel shall be white." - On two-lane, two-way roadways, the yellow center line markings shall be one of: (A) two-direction passing zone markings (normal width broken yellow line, passing permitted in either direction); (B) one-direction no-passing zone markings (double yellow line, one broken and one solid, passing permitted only for traffic adjacent to the broken line); or (C) two-direction no-passing zone markings (two normal width solid yellow lines, passing prohibited in either direction), as shown in Figure 3B-1. - "Except where a reversible lane (see Section 3B.04) or a two-way left-turn lane (see Section 3B.05) is present, the center line markings on undivided two-way roadways with four or more lanes for moving motor vehicle traffic always available shall be the two-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of normal width double solid yellow lines as shown in Figure 3B-2." Options (permitted): - Solid white lane line markings may be used: on approaches to intersections to separate contiguous through lanes; to separate through traffic lanes from auxiliary lanes (such as an added uphill truck lane); and on approaches to crosswalks across multi-lane roadways. - On shared-use paths wide enough for two minimum-width lanes, a solid yellow center line may be used to separate the two directions of travel where passing/traveling left of the line is not permitted, and a broken yellow center line may be used where passing is permitted. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 3B-2 shows a multi-lane two-way roadway where the double solid yellow center line separates the opposing directions (black arrows pointing opposite ways) while broken white lane lines separate same-direction lanes. [Image 2] Figure 3B-3 shows three-lane, two-way marking where the yellow center line (broken-plus-solid or double solid) divides opposing flows and a broken white line divides the two same-direction lanes. [Image 3] Figure 3B-1 shows two-lane, two-way applications with broken and solid yellow center lines defining passing and no-passing zones between opposing directions. [Image 4] Page 541 presents the full Figure 3B-2 with double yellow center lines between opposing multi-lane flows and white lane lines within each direction. [Image 5] Page 542 presents the full Figure 3B-3 illustrating one-direction and two-direction no-passing yellow center lines on a three-lane, two-way roadway. [Image 6] Page 595 shows a one-direction freeway/expressway where all lane separations for same-direction traffic are white (dotted/solid lane lines at a lane drop), with yellow appearing only as the left edge line. [Image 7] Page 674 shows tubular markers supplementing a double yellow center line (separating opposing directions) and white lane lines (separating same-direction lanes) at an unsignalized crosswalk. Citations: - Section 3B.01 Standard §1 (p.540) - Section 3B.06 Standard §1 (p.546) - Section 3B.01 Standard §4 (p.540) - Section 3B.01 Standard §6 (p.540) - Section 3B.06 Option §8 (p.548) - Section 9E.13 Option §1 (p.1106) - Figure 3B-1 (p.540) - Figure 3B-2 (p.541) - Figure 3B-3 (p.542) - Page 582 - Page 583 - Page 595 - Page 674
gold_answer: Yellow center lines separate lanes traveling in opposite directions. White lane lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction.
